Before I start giving my personal opinions on this, first a disclaimer: I might tend to complain a lot about what happens in the Ubuntu family of distros but that is because it is the distribution I use more then anything else. For any bad that I might mention, on any laptop or old PC or anything I've had a chance to play around with, Ubuntu has consistently been the one to work and always work while any other distribution I have tried is completely hit and miss. So overall my opinion of Ubuntu, despite any connections to Amazon or any controversy and despite the fact that I think Unity is utter crap, is that it is one of the best, if not, the best distro out there.

Now that that's out of the way, about KDE 5. I was very excited to try out the new release of Kubuntu shipping with KDE 5 as I thought it looks fantastic based on screenshots and I have heard that it is a lot speedier and more responsive. So I finally got around to installing it and all this is true! It seems very much like they are trying to copy the design of Lollipop for Android but I don't even care, it looks clean and neat and fresh and the old look is now immediately ugly in comparison. Although the only personal trouble I had with the new look is that it is very very white. So I decided to set darker colour schemes as I always do and this is where my troubles began.

This might seem like something small but when I have just freshly installed an OS and I am simply working on themes and shit, I don't want to face issues like this from the start. Go into settings>workspace theme and the first tab is 'look and feel'. This has a grand total of one option, Breeze. No link to download new options either, fair enough, KDE 5 is new, things like this are to be expected. So after considering my options I decided to go with 'Breeze' as my look and feel. The problem that I would soon find is that Breeze with any other option other then defaults doesn't seem to play very nicely. Next up, Desktop Theme. This changes the look of the Windows Explorer look-alike stuff, basically just the start bar and the start menu. Woot. Here I choose 'Breeze Dark'. Cursor theme, whatever. Splash Screen, once again a grand total of one option with no possibility of downloading new splash screens.

Next I move on to colour scheme, which inexplicably is separated from all the options I mentioned before into its own entry in general settings. Here I simply chose Breeze Dark once again, which seems to be exactly the same as Obsidian Coast with slightly different shades of colour. I'll play with the rest of the settings later. Back out I go into general settings and now icons. Breeze Dark again. All of these settings could quite easily be contained in one entry in my opinion and should be but thats another story.

So at this point I decide to get my torrents up and running again. I open my start menu and half of the icons have disappeared. Whatever, I'll sort that out later. Open Muon Software Center and it's looking nice and dark and fits perfectly with the rest of the UI, reminding me of one of the things that I love about KDE theming. It's so nice to see my favourite programs like Deluge and Firefox (especially Firefox after using the Windows version and the pathetic Android version) in a dark skin, looking good for a change without all that awful white and grey. So I download Deluge.

In the mean time I fire up Firefox and am greeted by a nice sleek dark looking browser without the need for any themes... not. The only thing to do with KDE themes that I chose are the window decorations. The close and maximize buttons and shit, that's it. Otherwise it now looks completely ugly and old and grey compared to the rest of the UI. How disappointing. By now Deluge has installed so I click on my first magnet link and fire up Deluge. Once again its got its old crappy gey and white ugly look with nice new shiny window decorations. KDE 5 is starting to feel like I've gone backwards..

But wait! Maybe I just need to reboot! I've just installed this thing and made a lot of changes, that's it, I'll reboot. I click reboot and am greeting by a white band across my screen. If I look closely I can make out some writing. White writing on a white background. Besides the fact that this style of dialogue option is a direct rip off from Windows 8 the theme has completely fucked it up. But I make out the reboot button, doing this will surely fix everything.. Nope. Still missing icons, still the ugly half old, half new looking programs like Firefox and still the almost completely unreadable power dialogue options.

Now this leads me to ask a few questions such as, what the hell is this doing in a LTS release? Besides the overall look and feel that only had the option of 'Breeze', I took the dark variant of Breeze for everything. Surely it's not unrealistic to think that others would choose all the same options as I did on the first time around? It's no brainer really which leads me to ask, do these people even test their own work? How is it even possible to end up with unreadable dialogues from choosing all the dark variants of the DEFAULT style? That can only be possible if they didn't even bother to test it. And if the only option for overall style is Breeze light, why even offer any other options at all. It's a complete mess.

I thought that I had moved onto Lollipop too soon for my device but using KDE 5 has made me realise what it really means to upgrade to something too soon. These might seem like small issues to some people but this is the skeleton, the structure of the OS. This is what leads to everything else working nicely. If I have to work around simple things that don't function properly from the very start, I'm already losing interest because I've got more important things to spend time on in Linux then making sure the fucking themes all work nicely together. And as I consider going with Gnome this time around it brings me to my main question. Was KDE 5 adopted by Kubuntu too soon?
Was KDE 5 added to Kubuntu too early (especially on a LTS release)?
Welcome to 8.10 Intrepid Ibex all over again? :-/
What happened with 8.10? My first taste of Linux was actually Ubuntu 9.10 lol so I missed that one by a year.

KDE 4 was under baked and buggy as hell. Upgrading from 8.04 to 8.10 was a disaster for many, and even clean installs of 8.10 refused to work on any computer I tried. I'm pretty sure Ubuntu was swapping in new guts at the time, like they do frequently, so that probably didn't make things easier. Things slowly improved starting with 9.04 Jaunty, but it took several releases.

I want to like KDE but I can't wrap my head around some of the ignored design flaws that have been there from the beginning.

No fully configurable autohide delay.

No vertical desktop switcher. No mini composited desktop thumbnails.

Kwallet has been a mess forever.

Widget interface instability.

Broken themes everywhere.

Wide vertical bar widget support is abysmal.

Gnome has none of these problems and uses less memory. I can't think of anything in KDE that is better than Gnome 3.14/3.16's current functionality with extensions.
On the other hand, unlike the current GNOME, the current KDE actually has a decent UI.

That's up to user preference though. There is a Gnome extension for just about everything, and it is no more difficult installing and configuring extensions than it is to tweak KDE. I actually find it easier to tweak Gnome when using the Gnome Tweak Tool.

I can get resizable composited dropdown thumbnails from an autohide top bar to keep track of anything I need. Live vertical autohide workspace switcher. You can't do those things in KDE.

I've actually really liked Gnome3 from the start. It's super efficient and speedy and actually a pleasure to work with. Thanks for confirming to me that I need to make the change. That just leaves me thinking, do I stay with Ubuntu or finally get into Debian?

Try Antergos. A fully set up Arch install blows Ubuntu/Debian out of the water. I don't have to search for Deb's, or RPM's, or tarballs, or repositories, or bang my head against a wall at unknown dependencies. If it could possibly work on Linux odds are it is in AUR and up to date.

Awesome I'll definitely check it out. Saw that Debian have finally released a new version so I grabbed that. Also got Ubuntu Gnome. The thing with Ubuntu is that everything always works properly the first time with little to no setup, from my specific keyboard model to my Xbox 360 controller, and that is hard to beat for any other distro. But I think it's time to do some shopping around again and to see what's what. I'll get hold of Antergos and maybe also take a look at how Fedora is these days. Maybe I'll even see how the other desktop environments are doing these days, like Enlightenment, I enjoyed Bodhi Linux a few years back when it was still new, I can only imagine it's much better now.

But yeah, for some reason I've mostly stuck to Debian based distros, I'm actually very keen to try something completely different like Arch.

If I could combine the desktop of KDE and the dash (or whatever the hell it's called) of Gnome, that would be my personal ultimate desktop environment. It's always been a split between the two for me. KDE for casual use (it looks pretty but is a mammoth as far as speed and efficiency goes) and Gnome for work (it's dash UI makes multitasking perfect and it can actually handle doing more then one thing at a time unlike KDE).
